**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good

- The G1 seam rule (`feature/g1_seam.rs`) and the trail walk (`feature/trail.rs`) are small, new files with provenance lines. The new code has no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()`. Lookups use `get` and `Option`.
- The output does not depend on the iteration order of the `HashMap`: components sort by their first edge, and chains sort by id and first edge.
- The rule is narrow: the same two patches (or one open-sheet rim), no other real feature edge at the vertex, and a turn of at most `CHAIN_TANGENT_DEG` (30 degrees). This is the same limit as the face rule.
- Old ids stay safe. A consumer that cannot resolve a saved chain id refuses with a named message (`selection.rs:136`, `selection.rs:351`: "... is no longer in the model: re-pick it"). It does not cut a different edge.
- No golden `.cl` or `.nc` file changes. No process files, no new dependency, no snapshot PNG.

## Results merged with main

Built and run locally (Windows, debug, `-j 6`) on a trial merge with `origin/main` at `a529c4553`. The merge was clean.

## Independent readings (local probe, not committed)

I ran `feature::chains` and `feature::edge_runs` on all fixtures in `testdata/models`, before (main) and after (this PR):

- Each feature edge is in exactly one chain, in all fixtures. Each chain walks connected. The length of a closed chain is the sum of its edges. Two calls give the same result.
- `fig8.step`: chains 1593 -> 877. The rim at z 19 now gives 3 closed chains (188.49 mm, 522.81 mm, 94.24 mm). Its runs are the same as the runs of the bottom rim at z 0. The `chains()` time is about 2x in debug (30.6 ms -> 65.4 ms). It does not grow faster than the edge count.
- These fixtures are unchanged: `Milling-test`, `Milling-test-inch`, `box`, `cube`, `bspline_dome`, and the lathe, modular and `tool_csys` fixtures.
- All old chain and run ids of `fig8`, `spline_revolved` and `sample_ap214` resolve to the same edges as before. No old id in any fixture resolves to a longer or a different edge set.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. The body does not name two fixtures that also change:
   - `fillet_corner.step`: chains 112 -> 109. Three times, a 26.875 mm line and 14 fillet chords of 0.35 mm (turns 3.2 and 6.4 degrees) now make one 16-edge chain. On main, the line and the first chord were one 2-edge chain, and the other 13 chords were separate. This is the intended result.
   - `sample_ap214.step`: two new 2-edge chains (`[1240,1246]`, `[1334,1336]`), on an open-sheet rim, 0.355 mm each, with a turn of 12.9 degrees.
   Please add these two lines to the readings.
2. On `fillet_corner.step`, 6 old multi-edge chain ids and 3 old run ids now resolve to `None`. A saved project with such a pick refuses with "... is no longer in the model: re-pick it". This is a visible refusal, not a wrong cut. But the body says "A saved chain selection that holds the id of one old piece still resolves". That is correct only for a one-edge id. Please add one sentence for the multi-edge case.
3. A patch joins faces less than 40 degrees apart. Thus a real corner of 30 degrees or less between two patches now joins into one chain. This agrees with the planar face rule (`CHAIN_TANGENT_DEG`). It is a note only.
4. `feature.rs` is 1544 lines (1550 on main). It is still over the 400-line limit. This PR makes it smaller.

Not exercised: the ui suites (the PR does not change `crates/ui`), the GUI, and the frame time of #2201.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
